question: In which year were the Indian Civil Service (ICS) and Indian Police (IP) replaced by the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), later recognised as All-India Services?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1947**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Civil Service (ICS) and Indian Police (IP) were replaced by the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** and **Indian Police Service (IPS)** in the year **1947**.
 
• The transition marked the establishment of the **All-India Services**, which aimed to maintain a unified administrative structure post-independence.
 
• The All-India Services, including IAS and IPS, are governed by the provisions of **Article 312** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• IAS officers are responsible for administrative roles and policy formulation, while IPS officers oversee law enforcement and public safety.
 
• This change symbolized the restructuring of administrative systems to align with the goals of a sovereign and democratic India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Civil Service (ICS):**

 
 
• The ICS was established during British rule in India and was considered the backbone of colonial administration.
 
• It primarily consisted of British officers, though Indians were allowed to join after 1922.
 
 
 
• **Indian Police (IP):**
 
 
• Similar to the ICS, the IP was the police force under British rule, tasked with maintaining law and order.
 
• Only a few Indian officers were recruited into the IP during colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Indian Administrative Service (IAS):**
 
 
• The IAS was established post-independence to replace the ICS and form a national administrative cadre.
 
• IAS officers are responsible for policy implementation, public administration, and governance across India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Police Service (IPS):**
 
 
• The IPS replaced the colonial Indian Police in 1947 to form a more democratic and efficient policing system.
 
• IPS officers are responsible for maintaining law and order, crime prevention, and implementing police reforms.
 
 
 
• **All-India Services:**
 
 
• The All-India Services consist of the IAS, IPS, and Indian Forest Service (IFS).
 
• The officers of these services hold positions both at the central and state levels, ensuring administrative continuity across the country.
 
• They are appointed by the President of India and serve under the central and state governments.
